chunks: And among what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Yaʿfur, who said:
I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who does not know whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or one. He said: He completes it with one rakʿah.

So the first point concerning these reports is that they do not contradict what we have previously presented, because those are many times more than these, and it is not permissible to turn away from the greater number to the lesser, as we have explained in more than one place.

And even if they were opposing them and equal to them, there would still be no contradiction in them, because there is nothing in any of these reports stating that the doubt occurred in the first and second rakʿahs of the obligatory prayers or the supererogatory prayers.

And when this is not present in the report, we interpret them as referring to the supererogatory prayers, because in our view there is no sahw in the supererogatory prayers, and the one praying may build on the lesser if he wishes and on the greater if he wishes, though building on the lesser is better.
So we have understood these reports according to what we mentioned regarding the supererogatory prayers, so that the reports do not contradict one another.

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man about whom the legal ruling is being asked
key_terms.السَّهْوَ: forgetfulness or doubt occurring in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الشَّكَّ: doubt regarding the number of rakʿahs performed
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports under juristic consideration
key_terms.الْبِنَاءُ عَلَى الْأَقَلِّ: to proceed on the basis of the lesser number counted
key_terms.رَكْعَةٍ: a unit of salat (prayer), here referring to completing the prayer with one more unit

ai.seo_question: How is a hadith about doubting between one and two rakʿahs reconciled with other rulings on sahw in prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on doubt in the number of rakʿahs prayed, stating that one who doubts between one and two completes with one rakʿah. The accompanying juristic explanation clarifies that such reports are understood as referring to supererogatory prayers, in which the worshipper may build on either the lesser or greater number, with building on the lesser being preferable.
